Accessible design is part of good design. Use these lessons with logos, nameplates, slides, posters, labels, diagrams, interfaces, and fabricated objects.

## What you will learn

- describe important images for people using screen readers;
- choose readable type and use text effects carefully;
- understand hue, saturation, value, opacity, and common colour models; and
- test contrast and output on screens, prints, and real materials.

## Lessons

::: {.ter-path-grid}
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 1. Access & Alt Text

Understand why accommodation matters and describe what an image contributes.

[Open the lesson](01-access-and-alt-text.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 2. Fonts & Text Effects

Compare typefaces, zoom out, and test backgrounds, outlines, shadows, and 3D effects.

[Open the lesson](02-fonts-and-text-effects.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 3. Understanding Colour

Connect human colour perception with hue, saturation, value, RGB, CMYK, and opacity.

[Open the lesson](03-understanding-colour.qmd)
:::
::: {.ter-path-card}
### 4. Contrast & Output

Use colour for emphasis without relying on colour alone, then test screen, print, and fabrication output.

[Open the lesson](04-contrast-and-output.qmd)
:::
:::

The lesson text is reorganized from the [Graphics Accommodation Guide](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AfDpLSJQtKy7YUMdwL8-BBR81NTv9Ck_cyzQ4pA2Hk4/edit). Source links and graphic descriptions are retained in the relevant lesson.
